quests.hint: This describes the feeling when your stomach is empty and you need to eat.
quests.explanation: 'Hungry' is an adjective: 'I feel hungry.' 'Starving' is a stronger informal version. 'Be hungry for' also means to strongly desire something non-food-related.
quests.textToSpeak: After skipping lunch, I was very ___ by the time dinner was ready.
quests.correctAnswer: After skipping lunch, I was very hungry by the time dinner was ready.

quests.hint: This describes the feeling when your body needs water or another liquid drink.
quests.explanation: 'Thirsty' is an adjective. 'Feel thirsty,' 'get thirsty,' and 'make someone thirsty' are common. Spicy food often makes people thirsty.
quests.textToSpeak: After the long run in the heat, I was extremely ___ and drank two glasses of water.
quests.correctAnswer: After the long run in the heat, I was extremely thirsty and drank two glasses of water.

quests.hint: This describes the state of wanting to sleep - when your eyes feel heavy.
quests.explanation: 'Sleepy' is an adjective meaning drowsy. 'Feel sleepy' is the most common structure. 'Sleepy' can also describe a quiet place: 'a sleepy little village.'
quests.textToSpeak: I felt very ___ after staying up late watching films the night before.
quests.correctAnswer: I felt very sleepy after staying up late watching films the night before.

quests.hint: This is a large road vehicle that carries passengers along fixed routes.
quests.explanation: 'Take the bus' or 'catch a bus' are the natural collocations. 'By bus' (method of travel) uses no article. 'Bus stop' is where you wait.
quests.textToSpeak: I catch the number fourteen ___ every morning to get to the office on time.
quests.correctAnswer: I catch the number fourteen bus every morning to get to the office on time.

quests.hint: This is a vehicle that travels on rails and is often the fastest way between cities.
quests.explanation: 'Take the train' or 'get the train' are most natural. 'By train' uses no article. 'Train station' or 'railway station' is where you board.
quests.textToSpeak: The fastest way to get to the city centre from here is by ___.
quests.correctAnswer: The fastest way to get to the city centre from here is by train.

quests.hint: This is a car with a driver that you hire to take you to your destination.
quests.explanation: 'Take a taxi,' 'get a taxi,' or 'call a taxi' are the natural collocations. 'Taxi rank' is where they wait. 'Taxi driver' or 'cab driver' refers to the person.
quests.textToSpeak: We decided to take a ___ because we had far too much luggage to carry.
quests.correctAnswer: We decided to take a taxi because we had far too much luggage to carry.

quests.hint: This word is added to requests to make them polite - essential in English social interaction.
quests.explanation: 'Please' goes at the end of a request ('Could you help me, please?') or after the verb ('Please sit down'). It softens any request and shows respect.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you pass me the salt, ___? I appreciate your help very much.
quests.correctAnswer: Could you pass me the salt, please? I appreciate your help very much.

quests.hint: This is the word you say when you have made a mistake or want to apologise to someone.
quests.explanation: 'I'm sorry' is the most common English apology. 'I'm so sorry' adds emphasis. 'Sorry!' said quickly is used for minor accidental things like bumping into someone.
quests.textToSpeak: I am so ___ that I am late - the traffic on the way here was terrible.
quests.correctAnswer: I am so sorry that I am late - the traffic on the way here was terrible.

quests.hint: This phrase is the response when someone thanks you - showing it was no trouble at all.
quests.explanation: 'You're welcome' is the standard response to 'thank you.' 'My pleasure' is a slightly warmer alternative. Both signal warmth and good manners.
quests.textToSpeak: You are very ___ - it was truly my pleasure to help you today.
quests.correctAnswer: You are very welcome - it was truly my pleasure to help you today.

quests.hint: This adverb means before the expected or usual time - ahead of schedule.
quests.explanation: 'Early' can be an adjective ('an early start') or adverb ('She arrived early'). 'Early morning,' 'early bird,' and 'arrive early' are common collocations.
quests.textToSpeak: She always arrives ___ to make sure she gets a good seat at the front.
quests.correctAnswer: She always arrives early to make sure she gets a good seat at the front.

quests.hint: This adverb means after the expected or usual time - not on time or delayed.
quests.explanation: 'Late' can be an adjective ('a late train') or adverb ('He arrived late'). 'Running late' means you are behind schedule. 'Better late than never' is a common saying.
quests.textToSpeak: He was running ___ and had to sprint to catch the last train of the evening.
quests.correctAnswer: He was running late and had to sprint to catch the last train of the evening.

quests.hint: This adverb means at a fast speed - doing something in a short amount of time.
quests.explanation: 'Quickly' is the adverb form of 'quick.' It modifies verbs: 'finish quickly,' 'leave quickly.' 'As quickly as possible' is a very useful English phrase.
quests.textToSpeak: She finished the whole assignment very ___ and still had time to check it.
quests.correctAnswer: She finished the whole assignment very quickly and still had time to check it.

quests.hint: This is a large open area of public green space where people can walk and relax.
quests.explanation: 'In the park' is the correct preposition. 'Go to the park,' 'walk in the park,' and 'visit the park' are common expressions. Parks are public and free.
quests.textToSpeak: On weekends, I enjoy taking my dog for a walk in the ___ near our house.
quests.correctAnswer: On weekends, I enjoy taking my dog for a walk in the park near our house.

quests.hint: This is a place where people sell and buy food, goods, and crafts, often outdoors.
quests.explanation: 'Market' can mean a food market, farmers' market, or stock market. 'At the market' or 'in the market' are both used. 'Go to market' means to sell commercially.
quests.textToSpeak: The local ___ sells fresh fruit, vegetables, and flowers every Saturday morning.
quests.correctAnswer: The local market sells fresh fruit, vegetables, and flowers every Saturday morning.

quests.hint: This is a shop where prescribed medicines and over-the-counter health products are sold.
quests.explanation: 'Pharmacy' is the formal word; 'chemist's' is the British informal term. 'At the pharmacy' or 'from the pharmacy' are the correct prepositions to use.
quests.textToSpeak: I need to collect my prescription from the ___ on the way home from work.
quests.correctAnswer: I need to collect my prescription from the pharmacy on the way home from work.

quests.hint: This is the first part of the day, from when you wake up until midday.
quests.explanation: 'In the morning' (general) vs 'this morning' (today). 'Morning person' means someone who is alert early. 'Good morning' is the standard greeting.
quests.textToSpeak: I prefer to exercise in the ___ when I feel most alert and energetic.
quests.correctAnswer: I prefer to exercise in the morning when I feel most alert and energetic.

quests.hint: This is the middle part of the day, between midday and early evening.
quests.explanation: 'In the afternoon' uses 'in' not 'at.' 'This afternoon,' 'this afternoon's meeting,' and 'afternoon tea' are all common British English expressions.
quests.textToSpeak: She has her piano lessons every Tuesday ___ after school finishes at three.
quests.correctAnswer: She has her piano lessons every Tuesday afternoon after school finishes at three.

quests.hint: This is the later part of the day, after work and before night-time.
quests.explanation: 'In the evening' uses 'in' not 'at.' 'This evening' means tonight. 'Evening class' and 'evening meal' are common compound nouns in British English.
quests.textToSpeak: In the ___, we usually relax and watch something on television together.
quests.correctAnswer: In the evening, we usually relax and watch something on television together.

quests.hint: This is the warm, bold colour of blood, fire engines, and ripe strawberries.
quests.explanation: 'Red' is used as an adjective before nouns ('a red car') or after verbs ('the car is red'). 'In red' means wearing or showing that colour.
quests.textToSpeak: She wore a stunning ___ dress to the dinner party on Saturday evening.
quests.correctAnswer: She wore a stunning red dress to the dinner party on Saturday evening.

quests.hint: This is the cool colour of a clear sky or the deep ocean on a sunny day.
quests.explanation: 'Blue' is both a colour adjective and a noun. 'Feel blue' informally means feel sad. 'Navy blue,' 'sky blue,' and 'royal blue' are common shades.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ sky was completely clear without a single cloud visible all day.
quests.correctAnswer: The blue sky was completely clear without a single cloud visible all day.

quests.hint: This is the colour of fresh grass, leaves, and plants - associated with nature.
quests.explanation: 'Green' can mean environmentally friendly ('going green'). 'Dark green' and 'light green' are useful shades. 'Green light' also means permission to proceed.
quests.textToSpeak: The hills were covered in lush ___ grass after all the recent heavy rain.
quests.correctAnswer: The hills were covered in lush green grass after all the recent heavy rain.

quests.hint: This is a round fruit, red or green in colour, crunchy and sweet or slightly sour.
quests.explanation: 'An apple' (with 'an' before a vowel sound). 'Apple juice,' 'apple pie,' and 'apple tree' are common compound nouns. One 'a day keeps the doctor away' is famous.
quests.textToSpeak: An ___ a day keeps the doctor away - or so the old saying tells us.
quests.correctAnswer: An apple a day keeps the doctor away - or so the old saying tells us.

quests.hint: This is the natural stimulant found in coffee, tea, and many soft drinks.
quests.explanation: 'Caffeine intake,' 'caffeine-free,' and 'sensitive to caffeine' are key collocations. Found naturally in coffee beans and tea leaves. 'Decaffeinated' means with the caffeine removed.
quests.textToSpeak: She stopped consuming ___ after realising it was seriously affecting her sleep.
quests.correctAnswer: She stopped consuming caffeine after realising it was seriously affecting her sleep.

quests.hint: This is the sweet white or brown substance added to food and drinks for sweetness.
quests.explanation: 'Sugar' is uncountable: 'add sugar,' 'a spoonful of sugar.' 'Cut down on sugar' (reduce your intake) and 'sugary drinks' are common health-related phrases.
quests.textToSpeak: The doctor strongly advised him to cut down on ___ for health reasons.
quests.correctAnswer: The doctor strongly advised him to cut down on sugar for health reasons.

quests.hint: This is someone you like very much and spend time with voluntarily - not family.
quests.explanation: 'Best friend,' 'close friend,' and 'make friends' are key collocations. 'Friend of mine' is more natural than 'my friend' when introducing someone to others.
quests.textToSpeak: She is my closest ___ - we have known each other since primary school.
quests.correctAnswer: She is my closest friend - we have known each other since primary school.

quests.hint: This is the person who lives next door or very close to your home.
quests.explanation: 'Neighbour' (British spelling) or 'neighbor' (American). 'Next-door neighbour' is very specific. 'Good neighbours' make daily life much more pleasant.
quests.textToSpeak: Our ___ always waters our plants when we go away on holiday.
quests.correctAnswer: Our neighbour always waters our plants when we go away on holiday.

quests.hint: This is someone who works with you at the same company or organisation.
quests.explanation: 'Colleague' is more formal than 'workmate' or 'coworker.' 'A colleague of mine' or 'my colleague' are both correct. It is used in professional contexts.
quests.textToSpeak: My ___ helped me finish the urgent report when I was running out of time.
quests.correctAnswer: My colleague helped me finish the urgent report when I was running out of time.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that costs very little money - great value.
quests.explanation: 'Cheap' can be positive ('great value') or slightly negative ('poor quality'). 'Cheap flight,' 'cheap meal,' and 'find something cheap' are all common collocations.
quests.textToSpeak: She found a very ___ flight online and booked it immediately before it sold out.
quests.correctAnswer: She found a very cheap flight online and booked it immediately before it sold out.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that is free from dirt, marks, or contamination.
quests.explanation: 'Clean' is both an adjective ('a clean room') and a verb ('clean the house'). 'Keep it clean,' 'clean up,' and 'squeaky clean' are common expressions.
quests.textToSpeak: Please keep the shared kitchen ___ so that everyone can use it comfortably.
quests.correctAnswer: Please keep the shared kitchen clean so that everyone can use it comfortably.

quests.hint: This adjective describes an environment or situation with very little noise.
quests.explanation: 'Quiet' describes both people ('a quiet person') and places ('a quiet street'). 'Keep quiet' means be silent. 'Peace and quiet' is a very common English phrase.
quests.textToSpeak: The library must be kept ___ so that everyone can concentrate properly.
quests.correctAnswer: The library must be kept quiet so that everyone can concentrate properly.
